_purpose: Phase 6A. Frozen holdout protocol to confirm (or not) the Phase-5B digital-shift result, and to separate its two possible causes: the cheaper randomisation itself, or SciPy's per-replicate engine construction. Committed before the study is run.

background.phase5_claim: random digital shifts had 0.09x the time-normalised MSE of SciPy-scrambled Sobol' (docs/PHASE5_SAMPLING_POLICY.md), on one 12-contract grid and one machine
background.erratum: Phases 3-5 called SciPy's scramble=True 'Owen scrambling'. It is Matousek's random linear matrix scrambling plus a digital shift (LMS+shift). Results are unaffected; the label was wrong.
background.new_arm: own implementation of the same LMS+shift randomisation on cached direction numbers (budget_policy.lms_uniforms), with per-replicate set-up of O(d log2 N) bit operations

randomisations.owen: SciPy qmc.Sobol(scramble=True), a new engine per replicate (key kept from Phase 5; it is LMS+shift)
randomisations.lms: own LMS+shift: random nonsingular lower-triangular binary matrix per coordinate applied to the generating matrix, points by doubling, digital shift, sub-2^-30 uniform jitter
randomisations.shift: digital shift (plus jitter) of one cached unscrambled Sobol' point set (Phase 5)

construction: path PCA (joint_greeks.pca_factor); estimator: CPW-first (Delta, Gamma, Vega) on shared points

grid.note: 24 scenarios. None of these m, K/S0, sigma, T or r values occurs in any earlier grid (Phases 2-5).

loss: equal-weight risk-vector loss: mean over Greeks of MSE_g / s_g^2, s_g = per-path sd of the plain-MC CPW-first estimator (2^16 paths per scenario)

equal_n.statistic: variance of replicate means (reference-free; all arms unbiased); ratios with 95% percentile bootstrap over replicates, geometric mean over scenarios per (m, N)

timed.order: the four strategies run back to back within each replication
timed.metric: time-normalised loss = loss x mean measured wall; ratios with 95% bootstrap, geometric mean over scenarios per (m, budget)

scheduler.rqmc: budget_policy.optimise_schedule with the arm's own calibrated cost model; an infeasible plan runs nothing and is recorded (no fallback, so the arms are compared as they are)
scheduler.mc: budget_policy.mc_schedule with blocks capped at asian_qmc.mc_block(m)
scheduler.cost_model: budget_policy.calibrate_cost_model(m, 'joint', randomisations = owen, lms, shift), at the start of the run

portable.role: second environment (e.g. a GitHub Actions runner via .github/workflows/phase6-portable.yml); 6 scenarios. Its equal-N part uses the same seeds as the holdout run, so those numbers should reproduce exactly on any machine with the same library versions.

hypotheses.A1: Implementation check: own LMS / SciPy LMS variance ratio has geometric mean in [0.9, 1.1] in every (m, N) cell (same randomisation, so equal variance in expectation).
hypotheses.A2: Per-point quality: at equal N >= 2^10 the digital shift alone has larger variance than LMS+shift (shift / LMS > 1 with the 95% CI above 1 in every (m, N) cell). Theory: scrambling, unlike a shift alone, can improve the convergence rate for smooth integrands.
hypotheses.A3: Replication of Phase 5B: at budgets <= 20 ms the shift has lower time-normalised loss than SciPy LMS (CI upper < 1), in every (m, budget) cell where SciPy LMS is feasible.
hypotheses.A4: Cause: own LMS is at least as efficient per unit time as the shift (geometric mean over all (m, budget) cells of LMS / shift <= 1, and every cell's CI upper bound <= 1.10). If A2 and A4 hold, the Phase-5 advantage was SciPy's per-replicate overhead, not the shift.
hypotheses.A5: Validity: pooled 95% coverage >= 0.93 for every RQMC arm; at most 5% of runs above 1.10 x budget in any feasible cell.
hypotheses.A6: Second environment (if run): equal-N numbers reproduce; the equal-time ranking of the arms is the same.
